publisher_scope_notice: Five Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary pages were directly opened on 2026-11-01. Their sense/POS/grammar observations are research, not independent exact-sense CEFR verification. Oxford topic tags and Cambridge indexed search snippets are NOT direct independent CEFR proof. No human review, British audio listening, physical iPhone QA or release is claimed.

records.original_english_definition: The pleasant feeling when worry, pain or difficulty ends.
records.original_burmese_meaning: စိတ်သက်သာရာရမှု
records.original_example_sentence: He felt relief when the missing bag was found.
records.source_supported_observation: Oxford directly distinguishes the emotional feeling of relief (sense 1) from pain reduction (sense 2) and humanitarian aid (sense 3). The frozen example demonstrates the emotional sense and is grammatical. Oxford's Feelings b2 topic tag is not independently verified exact-sense CEFR evidence.
records.suggested_myanmar_UNAPPROVED: စိုးရိမ်ပူပန်မှု ပျောက်ကင်းသွားသည့်အခါ ခံစားရသော စိတ်သက်သာမှု
records.suggested_example_UNAPPROVED: She felt a sense of relief when her brother arrived safely.
records.independent_reviewer_question: Confirm that the example, Myanmar gloss and intended emotional sense match; obtain independent exact-sense B2 publisher CEFR evidence.

records.original_english_definition: Refusal to accept or support a change or action.
records.original_burmese_meaning: ခုခံဆန့်ကျင်မှု
records.original_example_sentence: The proposal met resistance from local residents.
records.source_supported_observation: Oxford sense 1 explicitly covers opposition to a plan, idea or change. The frozen proposal/residents example is grammatical. Oxford tags Preferences and decisions c1 for this sense; this is a topic label, not direct independently reviewed CEFR proof and should trigger a B2-versus-C1 review rather than automatic releveling.
records.suggested_myanmar_UNAPPROVED: အစီအစဉ် သို့မဟုတ် အပြောင်းအလဲတစ်ခုကို ဆန့်ကျင်ကန့်ကွက်မှု
records.suggested_example_UNAPPROVED: The new policy faced strong resistance from local residents.
records.independent_reviewer_question: Independently resolve whether the exact opposition-to-change noun sense is B2 or C1; do not use the different verb resist B2 self-restraint sense as evidence.

records.original_english_definition: The business of selling goods directly to customers.
records.original_burmese_meaning: လက်လီရောင်းချမှု
records.original_example_sentence: She has worked in retail for five years.
records.source_supported_observation: Oxford directly defines retail as an uncountable noun for selling goods to the public, usually through shops, and contrasts it with wholesale. The frozen in-retail employment example is grammatical. Oxford Business b2 and Shopping b2 are topic tags, not independent exact-sense CEFR approval.
records.suggested_myanmar_UNAPPROVED: စားသုံးသူများထံ ကုန်ပစ္စည်းများကို လက်လီရောင်းချသည့်လုပ်ငန်း
records.suggested_example_UNAPPROVED: My sister works in retail at a clothing shop.
records.independent_reviewer_question: Check the noun business-sector sense, Burmese idiomatic precision and independent exact-sense CEFR classification.

records.original_english_definition: A painful feeling of embarrassment or guilt.
records.original_burmese_meaning: အရှက်ကွဲမှု၊ အရှက်ရမှု
records.original_example_sentence: He felt shame after lying to his friend.
records.source_supported_observation: Oxford sense 1 a shame means something disappointing; sense 2 uncountable shame means embarrassment or guilt about one's action. The frozen lying-to-a-friend example targets sense 2 and is grammatical. The Myanmar word အရှက်ကွဲမှု can imply public loss of face rather than private guilt, so a fluent reviewer should refine it.
records.suggested_myanmar_UNAPPROVED: မိမိလုပ်ရပ်ကြောင့် ရှက်ရွံ့ပြီး အပြစ်ရှိသလို ခံစားရမှု
records.suggested_example_UNAPPROVED: She felt shame after lying to her friend.
records.independent_reviewer_question: Review whether the proposed Myanmar gloss conveys internal shame rather than public disgrace; retain a noun example if POS remains noun.

records.original_english_definition: To a limited degree; rather than completely.
records.original_burmese_meaning: အတော်အသင့်၊ တစ်စိတ်တစ်ပိုင်း
records.original_example_sentence: The second proposal is somewhat more practical.
records.source_supported_observation: Oxford describes somewhat as a rather formal adverb meaning to some degree, with examples modifying adjectives or a situation. The frozen somewhat more practical sentence is grammatical. Burmese တစ်စိတ်တစ်ပိုင်း may suggest an object's physical part instead of the intended degree of practicality.
records.suggested_myanmar_UNAPPROVED: အတန်အသင့်၊ အနည်းငယ်
records.suggested_example_UNAPPROVED: The updated plan is somewhat easier to follow.
records.independent_reviewer_question: Confirm degree-modifier sense, formal register, fluent Myanmar and independently sourced exact-sense CEFR.
